Here \(n = 8\) and \(\sum x_i = 4+7+8+9+10+12+13+17 = 80\), so the mean is \(\bar{x} = \frac{80}{8} = 10\).

The absolute deviations \(\lvert x_i - 10 \rvert\) are \(6,\ 3,\ 2,\ 1,\ 0,\ 2,\ 3,\ 7\), whose sum is \(\sum \lvert x_i - \bar{x} \rvert = 24\).

Hence \(\text{M.D.}(\bar{x}) = \frac{1}{n}\sum \lvert x_i - \bar{x} \rvert = \frac{24}{8} = 3\).

Here \(n = 10\) and \(\sum x_i = 38+70+48+40+42+55+63+46+54+44 = 500\), so \(\bar{x} = \frac{500}{10} = 50\) (which lies inside the range \(38\) to \(70\), as it must).

The absolute deviations \(\lvert x_i - 50 \rvert\) are \(12,\ 20,\ 2,\ 10,\ 8,\ 5,\ 13,\ 4,\ 4,\ 6\), whose sum is \(\sum \lvert x_i - \bar{x} \rvert = 84\).

Hence \(\text{M.D.}(\bar{x}) = \frac{84}{10} = 8.4\).

Arrange the \(n = 12\) observations in ascending order:

\(10,\ 11,\ 11,\ 12,\ 13,\ 13,\ 14,\ 16,\ 16,\ 17,\ 17,\ 18\)

Since \(n\) is even, the median is the mean of the \(6^{\text{th}}\) and \(7^{\text{th}}\) observations:

\(M = \frac{13 + 14}{2} = 13.5\)

The absolute deviations \(\lvert x_i - 13.5 \rvert\) in the sorted order are \(3.5,\ 2.5,\ 2.5,\ 1.5,\ 0.5,\ 0.5,\ 0.5,\ 2.5,\ 2.5,\ 3.5,\ 3.5,\ 4.5\), whose sum is \(\sum \lvert x_i - M \rvert = 28\).

Hence \(\text{M.D.}(M) = \frac{28}{12} = \frac{7}{3} \approx 2.33\).

Arrange the \(n = 10\) observations in ascending order:

\(36,\ 42,\ 45,\ 46,\ 46,\ 49,\ 51,\ 53,\ 60,\ 72\)

Since \(n\) is even, the median is the mean of the \(5^{\text{th}}\) and \(6^{\text{th}}\) observations:

\(M = \frac{46 + 49}{2} = 47.5\)

The absolute deviations \(\lvert x_i - 47.5 \rvert\) in the sorted order are \(11.5,\ 5.5,\ 2.5,\ 1.5,\ 1.5,\ 1.5,\ 3.5,\ 5.5,\ 12.5,\ 24.5\), whose sum is \(\sum \lvert x_i - M \rvert = 70\).

Hence \(\text{M.D.}(M) = \frac{70}{10} = 7\).

Here \(N = \sum f_i = 26\), which is even, so the median is the mean of the \(13^{\text{th}}\) and \(14^{\text{th}}\) observations. The cumulative frequencies are \(8,\ 14,\ 16,\ 18,\ 20,\ 26\); both the \(13^{\text{th}}\) and the \(14^{\text{th}}\) observation fall in the class with cumulative frequency \(14\), i.e. both equal \(7\). Hence \(M = 7\).

| \(x_i\) | \(f_i\) | c.f. | \(\lvert x_i-M\rvert\) | \(f_i\lvert x_i-M\rvert\) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 5 | 8 | 8 | 2 | 16 |
| 7 | 6 | 14 | 0 | 0 |
| 9 | 2 | 16 | 2 | 4 |
| 10 | 2 | 18 | 3 | 6 |
| 12 | 2 | 20 | 5 | 10 |
| 15 | 6 | 26 | 8 | 48 |
| Total | 26 | | | 84 |

Hence \(\text{M.D.}(M) = \frac{84}{26} = \frac{42}{13} \approx 3.23\).

Here \(N = \sum f_i = 29\), which is odd, so the median is the \(\left(\frac{29+1}{2}\right)^{\text{th}} = 15^{\text{th}}\) observation. The cumulative frequencies are \(3,\ 8,\ 14,\ 21,\ 29\); the \(15^{\text{th}}\) observation lies in the class with cumulative frequency \(21\), so \(M = 30\).

| \(x_i\) | \(f_i\) | c.f. | \(\lvert x_i-M\rvert\) | \(f_i\lvert x_i-M\rvert\) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 15 | 3 | 3 | 15 | 45 |
| 21 | 5 | 8 | 9 | 45 |
| 27 | 6 | 14 | 3 | 18 |
| 30 | 7 | 21 | 0 | 0 |
| 35 | 8 | 29 | 5 | 40 |
| Total | 29 | | | 148 |

Hence \(\text{M.D.}(M) = \frac{148}{29} \approx 5.1\).

Here \(n = 8\) and \(\sum x_i = 6+7+10+12+13+4+8+12 = 72\), so \(\bar{x} = \frac{72}{8} = 9\).

The squared deviations \((x_i - 9)^2\) are \(9,\ 4,\ 1,\ 9,\ 16,\ 25,\ 1,\ 9\), whose sum is \(\sum (x_i-\bar{x})^2 = 74\).

Hence \(\sigma^2 = \frac{1}{n}\sum (x_i-\bar{x})^2 = \frac{74}{8} = 9.25\).

So the mean is \(9\) and the variance is \(9.25\).

The observations are \(1, 2, 3, \ldots, n\). Using \(\sum x_i = \frac{n(n+1)}{2}\),

\(\bar{x} = \frac{1}{n}\cdot\frac{n(n+1)}{2} = \frac{n+1}{2}\)

Using \(\sum x_i^2 = \frac{n(n+1)(2n+1)}{6}\) and \(\sigma^2 = \frac{1}{n}\sum x_i^2 - \bar{x}^2\),

\(\sigma^2 = \frac{(n+1)(2n+1)}{6} - \frac{(n+1)^2}{4} = \frac{n+1}{12}\big[2(2n+1) - 3(n+1)\big] = \frac{(n+1)(n-1)}{12}\)

So the mean is \(\frac{n+1}{2}\) and the variance is \(\frac{n^2-1}{12}\).

Let the two remaining observations be \(x\) and \(y\). With \(n = 8\) and \(\bar{x} = 9\),

\(\sum x_i = 8\times 9 = 72\), and the six known observations sum to \(6+7+10+12+12+13 = 60\), so \(x + y = 12\).

From \(\sigma^2 = \frac{1}{n}\sum x_i^2 - \bar{x}^2\),

\(\sum x_i^2 = n(\sigma^2 + \bar{x}^2) = 8(9.25 + 81) = 8\times 90.25 = 722\)

The six known squares sum to \(36+49+100+144+144+169 = 642\), so \(x^2 + y^2 = 80\).

Then \(2xy = (x+y)^2 - (x^2+y^2) = 144 - 80 = 64\), so \(xy = 32\), and \(x, y\) are the roots of

\(t^2 - 12t + 32 = 0 \Rightarrow (t-4)(t-8) = 0\)

Hence the remaining two observations are \(4\) and \(8\).

Let the two remaining observations be \(x\) and \(y\). With \(n = 7\) and \(\bar{x} = 8\),

\(\sum x_i = 7\times 8 = 56\), and the five known observations sum to \(2+4+10+12+14 = 42\), so \(x + y = 14\).

From \(\sigma^2 = \frac{1}{n}\sum x_i^2 - \bar{x}^2\),

\(\sum x_i^2 = 7(16 + 64) = 7\times 80 = 560\)

The five known squares sum to \(4+16+100+144+196 = 460\), so \(x^2 + y^2 = 100\).

Then \(2xy = (x+y)^2 - (x^2+y^2) = 196 - 100 = 96\), so \(xy = 48\), and \(x, y\) are the roots of

\(t^2 - 14t + 48 = 0 \Rightarrow (t-6)(t-8) = 0\)

Hence the remaining two observations are \(6\) and \(8\).

Let the observations be \(x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_6\) with \(\bar{x} = 8\) and \(\sigma = 4\), and let the new observations be \(y_i = 3x_i\).

New mean: \(\bar{y} = \frac{1}{6}\sum 3x_i = 3\bar{x} = 3\times 8 = 24\).

New variance: \(\frac{1}{6}\sum (y_i - \bar{y})^2 = \frac{1}{6}\sum 9(x_i - \bar{x})^2 = 9\sigma^2\), so the new standard deviation is \(3\sigma = 3\times 4 = 12\).

Hence the new mean is \(24\) and the new standard deviation is \(12\).

Let \(y_i = ax_i\) for \(i = 1, 2, \ldots, n\), where \(a \neq 0\).

Mean: \(\bar{y} = \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n} y_i = \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n} ax_i = a\cdot\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n} x_i = a\bar{x}\).

Variance: using \(\bar{y} = a\bar{x}\),

\(\text{Var}(y) = \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n} (y_i - \bar{y})^2 = \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n} (ax_i - a\bar{x})^2 = \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n} a^2(x_i - \bar{x})^2\)

\(= a^2\cdot\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n} (x_i - \bar{x})^2 = a^2\sigma^2\)

Hence the mean and variance of \(ax_1, ax_2, \ldots, ax_n\) are \(a\bar{x}\) and \(a^2\sigma^2\) respectively.

For the original \(n = 20\) observations with \(\bar{x} = 10\) and \(\sigma = 2\):

\(\sum x_i = 20\times 10 = 200\) and \(\sum x_i^2 = n(\sigma^2 + \bar{x}^2) = 20(4 + 100) = 2080\).

Omitting the incorrect observation \(8\) leaves \(n = 19\) observations with

\(\sum x_i = 200 - 8 = 192\) and \(\sum x_i^2 = 2080 - 64 = 2016\).

Correct mean: \(\bar{x} = \frac{192}{19} \approx 10.11\).

Correct variance: \(\sigma^2 = \frac{2016}{19} - \left(\frac{192}{19}\right)^2 = \frac{2016\times 19 - 192^2}{361} = \frac{38304 - 36864}{361} = \frac{1440}{361} \approx 3.99\).

Correct standard deviation: \(\sigma = \frac{12\sqrt{10}}{19} \approx 2.00\) (more precisely \(1.997\)).

Hence the correct mean is \(\frac{192}{19} \approx 10.11\) and the correct standard deviation is approximately \(1.997\).

For the original \(n = 20\) observations with \(\bar{x} = 10\) and \(\sigma = 2\):

\(\sum x_i = 200\) and \(\sum x_i^2 = 20(4 + 100) = 2080\).

Replacing the incorrect observation \(8\) by \(12\) keeps \(n = 20\) and gives

\(\sum x_i = 200 - 8 + 12 = 204\) and \(\sum x_i^2 = 2080 - 64 + 144 = 2160\).

Correct mean: \(\bar{x} = \frac{204}{20} = 10.2\).

Correct variance: \(\sigma^2 = \frac{2160}{20} - (10.2)^2 = 108 - 104.04 = 3.96\).

Correct standard deviation: \(\sigma = \sqrt{3.96} = \frac{3\sqrt{11}}{5} \approx 1.99\).

Hence the correct mean is \(10.2\) and the correct standard deviation is approximately \(1.99\).

For the original \(n = 100\) observations with \(\bar{x} = 20\) and \(\sigma = 3\):

\(\sum x_i = 100\times 20 = 2000\) and \(\sum x_i^2 = n(\sigma^2 + \bar{x}^2) = 100(9 + 400) = 40900\).

Omit the three incorrect observations \(21, 21, 18\). Their sum is \(60\) and the sum of their squares is \(441 + 441 + 324 = 1206\), so for the remaining \(n = 97\) observations

\(\sum x_i = 2000 - 60 = 1940\) and \(\sum x_i^2 = 40900 - 1206 = 39694\).

Mean: \(\bar{x} = \frac{1940}{97} = 20\).

Variance: \(\sigma^2 = \frac{39694}{97} - 20^2 = \frac{39694 - 38800}{97} = \frac{894}{97} \approx 9.22\).

Standard deviation: \(\sigma = \sqrt{\frac{894}{97}} \approx 3.04\).

Hence the mean is \(20\) and the standard deviation is approximately \(3.04\).
